ctx.x: I want you to feel as if you know me 59 years. Alright. Of course I'm only 39 years old. Jack Benny and I. This is my chair. This is where I sit and look at the TV. And lately I haven't been getting Channel 4, so I called Burt. He's in the TV business now since he's got his children growing up. He doesn't play much music. He's a Saturday nighter.

items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: With the exception of Johnny's trumpet playing, there's nothing of merit in the show. And there's eight acts including Jack Benny and all of them.

ctx.x: You know how I used to- What years was this now, you're talking about all these four trumpets and three trombones?

Oh, in the forties, in the forties, up to fifty-nine. We used as many men as we could. We tried to engage those men for the whole season. So you'd be sure you have them. You'd give them all the dates, and I'd make them sign it, but they accepted the dates. See? Then you have, by the time after you play one or two balls, you've got an organized orchestra, because they're good musicians. And they save you a lot of trouble. You don't do a lot of talking. They know what you're going to do, you know what I mean? And…
What do you remember about singers singing to the megaphone? Do you remember much about that period?
